cardiovascular-physiology: The heart has four chambers, and the left ventricle wall is about three times thicker than the right.
The sinoatrial (SA) node is the heart's natural pacemaker, firing 60 to 100 times per minute at rest.
Stroke volume equals end-diastolic volume minus end-systolic volume, about 70 mL per beat.
Cardiac output equals heart rate times stroke volume, about 5 liters per minute at rest.
Hypertension is called a silent killer because it usually causes no symptoms while damaging organs.
cell-respiration: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm and yields a net 2 ATP, 2 NADH, and 2 pyruvate per glucose without requiring oxygen.
The citric acid cycle turns twice per glucose, and each turn produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 ATP (or GTP), and 2 CO2.
Most ATP is made by ATP synthase, driven by a proton gradient that the electron transport chain builds across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain and is reduced to water at Complex IV.
Fermentation makes no extra ATP beyond glycolysis; it only regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue without oxygen.
chemical-equilibrium: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic: the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.
The equilibrium constant K depends only on temperature.
If Q is less than K the reaction proceeds forward, and if Q is greater than K it proceeds in reverse.
Le Chatelier's principle states that an equilibrium shifts in the direction that partially counteracts a change in conditions.
A catalyst speeds up reaching equilibrium but does not change the position of equilibrium or the value of K.
contract-formation: A binding contract traditionally requires offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations, capacity, and certainty of terms.
An invitation to treat, such as goods displayed in a shop, is not an offer but an invitation to receive offers.
Under the mirror image rule, an acceptance must match the offer exactly, and a response changing the terms is a counter-offer.
Consideration must be sufficient but need not be adequate, and past consideration is not good consideration.
A contract may be void or voidable because of misrepresentation, mistake, duress, undue influence, or illegality.
ecology-course-reader: The carrying capacity, symbolized K, is the maximum population size that a particular environment can sustain over the long term.
Gause's competitive exclusion principle holds that two species competing for exactly the same limiting resources cannot coexist indefinitely in the same place.
Roughly 10 percent of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next, according to the ten percent rule.
Energy flows through ecosystems in one direction, whereas chemical elements cycle repeatedly between organisms and the nonliving environment.
Habitat loss is considered the single greatest threat to biodiversity worldwide.
ethical-theories: Consequentialism holds that the rightness of an action depends only on its consequences.
Classical utilitarianism, associated with Bentham and Mill, says the right action produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number.
Kant's categorical imperative includes the Formula of Universal Law and the Formula of Humanity, which forbids treating people merely as a means.
Aristotle's virtue ethics centres on eudaimonia and describes many virtues as a mean between two vices.
Contractualism grounds morality in agreement, as in Rawls's veil of ignorance and Scanlon's principles that no one could reasonably reject.
frankenstein-analysis: Frankenstein was first published anonymously in London on 1 January 1818 in three volumes.
The novel originated in a ghost-story contest proposed by Lord Byron at the Villa Diodati in 1816.
The novel uses a nested frame narrative of Robert Walton, Victor Frankenstein, and the creature.
The subtitle The Modern Prometheus refers to the Titan who stole fire from the gods and was punished.
The creature is never given a name in the novel.
hash-tables: A hash table uses a hash function to map keys to bucket indices, giving average O(1) insertion, lookup, and deletion.
Collisions occur when different keys map to the same bucket and are resolved by separate chaining or open addressing.
The load factor is the ratio of stored entries to buckets, and Java's HashMap uses a default maximum load factor of 0.75.
Doubling the table size on each resize makes insertion take amortized O(1) time.
In the worst case, when many keys collide, hash table operations degrade to O(n).
human-nutrition: Carbohydrate and protein provide about 4 kcal per gram, while fat provides about 9 kcal per gram.
The RDA for protein for healthy adults is 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight per day.
The fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E and K, while vitamin C and the B vitamins are water-soluble.
Most digestion and absorption occur in the small intestine, whose villi and microvilli greatly increase its absorptive surface area.
Dietary fibre is plant carbohydrate that human enzymes cannot digest, and adults are commonly advised to eat about 25 to 30 grams per day.
hypothesis-testing: The null hypothesis is the default claim of no effect and always contains an equality.
The p-value is the probability, assuming the null hypothesis is true, of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.
If the p-value is less than or equal to the significance level alpha, the null hypothesis is rejected.
The probability of a Type I error equals alpha, and power equals 1 minus beta, the probability of a Type II error.
The t-distribution was published in 1908 by William Sealy Gosset under the pen name Student.
industrial-revolution: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in roughly the 1760s and shifted production from hand work to machines and factories.
Cotton textiles were the leading sector, transformed by inventions such as the spinning jenny, water frame, spinning mule, and power loom.
James Watt patented the separate condenser in 1769, making steam engines far more fuel-efficient than Newcomen's design.
The Liverpool and Manchester Railway, opened in 1830, was the first intercity line operated entirely by steam locomotives.
Rapid urbanization brought poor housing, epidemics, and harsh factory labor, prompting reforms such as the Factory Act of 1833.
linear-algebra-basics: The product AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B.
Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so in general AB does not equal BA.
The determinant of a 2 x 2 matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d) is ad - bc.
A square matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is nonzero.
An eigenvector v of A satisfies Av = λv, and eigenvalues are found by solving det(A - λI) = 0.
memory-and-learning: Memory involves three processes: encoding, storage, and retrieval.
Short-term memory has limited capacity, about seven plus or minus two items per Miller or about four per Cowan.
Patient H.M. lost the ability to form new declarative memories after removal of most of his hippocampus but could still learn motor skills.
Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve shows rapid forgetting at first that then levels off.
Retrieval practice and spaced practice were rated as high-utility study techniques.
music-theory-fundamentals: Two notes an octave apart differ in frequency by a factor of two, and twelve half steps make up one octave.
The major scale follows the pattern of whole and half steps W-W-H-W-W-W-H.
A triad is built by stacking two thirds above a root and comes in major, minor, diminished, and augmented qualities.
In a time signature, the top number gives the beats per measure and the bottom number gives the note value that receives one beat.
The authentic cadence, moving from V to I, is the strongest and most conclusive ending in tonal music.
newtonian-mechanics: Newton's first law states that an object keeps its state of rest or uniform straight-line motion unless a net external force acts on it.
Newton's second law states that net force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma), with force measured in newtons.
Newton's third law says forces come in equal and opposite pairs that act on different objects.
The coefficient of kinetic friction is usually smaller than the coefficient of static friction.
Impulse equals change in momentum, and total momentum is conserved when no net external force acts on a system.
plate-tectonics: Tectonic plates are pieces of rigid lithosphere that move over the weak asthenosphere at about 2 to 10 cm per year.
Plate boundaries are divergent, convergent, or transform.
Seafloor spreading, proposed by Harry Hess, creates new oceanic crust at mid-ocean ridges and is recorded by symmetric magnetic stripes.
Slab pull is generally considered the strongest force driving plate motion.
Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift and the supercontinent Pangaea in 1912, but it was rejected for lack of a mechanism.
separation-of-powers: Montesquieu argued in The Spirit of the Laws (1748) that liberty disappears when lawmaking, executing, and judging powers are united in the same body.
The legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out, and the judiciary interprets and applies them to cases.
Checks and balances give each branch some ability to limit the others, through tools such as vetoes, impeachment, budget control, and confirmation of appointments.
Judicial review is the power of courts to declare laws and government actions invalid if they conflict with the constitution.
Federalism divides power vertically between a national government and regional governments, both of which derive authority from the constitution.
stellar-evolution: Stars form inside cold, dense giant molecular clouds composed mostly of molecular hydrogen.
Objects below about 0.08 solar masses never fuse hydrogen and become brown dwarfs.
More massive stars fuse hydrogen faster and therefore live much shorter lives; the Sun's main-sequence lifetime is about 10 billion years.
Stars from about 0.08 to 8 solar masses end as white dwarfs, which are supported by electron degeneracy pressure up to the Chandrasekhar limit of about 1.4 solar masses.
Stars above about 8 solar masses explode as core-collapse supernovae and leave behind neutron stars or black holes.
supply-demand-elasticity: The law of demand states that as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls, other things equal.
Equilibrium occurs at the price where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.
A change in a good's own price causes a movement along the curve, while changes in other determinants shift the curve.
When demand is inelastic, raising the price increases total revenue; when demand is elastic, it reduces total revenue.
A binding price ceiling below equilibrium causes a shortage, and a binding price floor above equilibrium causes a surplus.
tcp-ip-networking: The TCP/IP model has four layers: link, internet, transport and application.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long while an IPv6 address is 128 bits long.
TCP establishes a connection with a three-way handshake of SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK.
TCP flow control uses the receiver's advertised window, while congestion control uses a congestion window with slow start and AIMD.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses through a hierarchy of root, top-level domain and authoritative name servers, with caching governed by TTL values.
